foundations.title: What OpenRiak KV is
foundations.scope: Introduce the system's major components and the responsibilities shared between the database and the application.

foundations.title: Where OpenRiak fits
foundations.scope: Explain suitable workloads, strengths, and trade-offs that make other workloads a poor fit. Consolidate “Why OpenRiak” and “Use cases”.

foundations.title: From Dynamo and Riak to OpenRiak
foundations.scope: Explain the design's origins and evolution. Replace the lengthy reproduction of the Dynamo paper with an OpenRiak-focused explanation and links to the source material.

foundations.title: Rings, partitions, and virtual nodes
foundations.scope: Explain data distribution and the distinction between logical partitions and physical nodes. Combine the overlapping ring and vnode explanations.

foundations.title: The lifecycle of a read and a write
foundations.scope: Trace a request through the client, coordinator, replicas, storage, and response to establish a common mental model.

foundations.title: Replica placement and failure domains
foundations.scope: Explain preference lists, primary and fallback replicas, placement constraints, and resilience to node or location failures.

foundations.title: Membership, gossip, and handoff
foundations.scope: Explain how nodes learn about membership and how ownership and data move when a cluster changes.

foundations.title: Objects, keys, and buckets
foundations.scope: Explain the data model, object boundaries, metadata, and the consequences for application modelling.

foundations.title: Bucket types and data policies
foundations.scope: Explain namespaces, shared behaviour, and how bucket properties express data policies.

foundations.title: Eventual consistency and convergence
foundations.scope: Describe the promises, observable behaviour, and conditions required for convergence.

foundations.title: Quorums, availability, and durability
foundations.scope: Explain replication counts, read and write acknowledgements, primary requirements, and durable writes. Avoid implying that quorum settings alone provide strong consistency.

foundations.title: Causality, version vectors, and siblings
foundations.scope: Consolidate causal-context and vector explanations. Explain how the system distinguishes later changes from concurrent changes.

foundations.title: Resolving concurrent updates
foundations.scope: Explain application merging, last-write-wins policies, siblings, and information preservation. Consolidate the conflict-resolution and merge-strategy material.

foundations.title: Conflict-free replicated data types
foundations.scope: Explain convergence, supported operations, and the constraints on application semantics.

foundations.title: Conditional updates and latch objects
foundations.scope: Explain how these mechanisms reduce conflicts, their failure boundaries, and the limits of latch-based coordination.

foundations.title: Deletion, tombstones, and expiration
foundations.scope: Connect logical deletion, retention, reaping, expiration, and the risk of deleted data reappearing. Consolidate the two deletion explanations.

foundations.title: Secondary indexes and projected attributes
foundations.scope: Explain index terms, application representations, projections, and the storage and write costs of indexing.

foundations.title: How distributed queries execute
foundations.scope: Explain how scans, filters, combined queries, accumulation, and collation operate across virtual nodes.

foundations.title: Query consistency and snapshots
foundations.scope: Explain index visibility, vnode snapshots, and the boundaries of consistency across a distributed query.

foundations.title: Query cost and result delivery
foundations.scope: Explain selectivity, fan-out, buffering, pagination, and synchronous or asynchronous delivery. Consolidate query-performance material here.

foundations.title: Read repair and TicTac anti-entropy
foundations.scope: Explain divergence and the relationship between reactive and background repair. Maintain one current explanation of active anti-entropy.

foundations.title: Replication sources, queues, and sinks
foundations.scope: Explain the pipeline, object references, triggers, priorities, consumers, and backpressure. Consolidate the small component pages.

foundations.title: Real-time replication and fullsync
foundations.scope: Explain how the two mechanisms complement one another, including discovery, transport, and catching up after interruptions.

foundations.title: Multi-cluster topologies and behaviour
foundations.scope: Explain directional, active-active, and cascading arrangements, replication lag, concurrency, and metadata that remains local.

foundations.title: Targeted reconciliation and AAE folds
foundations.scope: Explain work bounded by bucket, key range, or time, and how it differs from full reconciliation.

foundations.title: Replication generations and compatibility
foundations.scope: Explain the architectural and migration differences between next-generation replication and legacy riak_repl v2/v3.

foundations.title: Storage backend trade-offs
foundations.scope: Provide a version-specific comparison of backend choices, distinguishing current recommendations from legacy behaviour.

foundations.title: How Bitcask stores data
foundations.scope: Explain append-only storage, the in-memory key directory, reads, merges, and resource implications. Link to separate configuration and maintenance procedures.

foundations.title: How Leveled stores data
foundations.scope: Explain the journal, ledger, caches, snapshots, and compaction, connecting them to read, write, and index behaviour.

foundations.title: Multiple backends and prefix routing
foundations.scope: Explain why data is routed to different backends and the implications of changing routing policies.

foundations.title: Persistence, filesystems, and space reclamation
foundations.scope: Explain buffering, persistence, filesystem behaviour, merges, and compaction. Distinguish storage reclamation from Erlang garbage collection.

foundations.title: Latency, queues, and resource contention
foundations.scope: Explain how vnode queues, Erlang scheduling, network and disk contention affect tail latency, overload, and recovery.

foundations.title: Capacity and growth
foundations.scope: Connect replicas, keys, values, indexes, caches, and recovery headroom to resource needs. Put sizing procedures in How-to.

foundations.title: Failure and recovery
foundations.scope: Explain transient failures, failed nodes, lost storage, and the assumptions behind repair, replacement, and recovery.

foundations.title: Backups, restores, and disaster recovery
foundations.scope: Explain what a distributed backup captures, its consistency limits, and the differences between backup, replication, and recovery.

foundations.title: Rolling maintenance and recovery headroom
foundations.scope: Explain how taking nodes out of service affects availability, background work, and capacity.

foundations.title: Mixed versions, capabilities, and upgrade boundaries
foundations.scope: Connect capability negotiation, mixed-version operation, activation, upgrade and downgrade boundaries, and rollback limits.

foundations.title: Security boundaries and trust
foundations.scope: Identify clients, administrators, nodes, and remote clusters, and explain which mechanisms protect each boundary.

foundations.title: Identities, authentication, and permissions
foundations.scope: Explain how users, groups, authentication sources, and permissions combine to make access decisions.

foundations.title: TLS and certificate trust
foundations.scope: Explain encryption, identity validation, and certificate trust relationships.
